handoff.purpose: Contains claim_text, candidate_names, and judge functions that parse and evaluate findings against module symbol indexes.

symbols.name: claim_text
symbols.note: Strips a '<where> | <severity> | ...' prefix from a finding's text. Returns the text after the second '|' if the second part is a known severity; otherwise returns the raw string.

symbols.name: candidate_names
symbols.note: Extracts candidate symbol names from a string using the module-level regex _NAME. Returns a set of non-empty captures.

symbols.name: judge
symbols.note: Determines whether a finding is provably wrong about the repository. Returns one of 'false', 'false-elsewhere', 'scoped', or 'undecided' with a reason string.

claims.text: The assertion, with any ``<where> | <severity> | ...`` prefix stripped.
claims.why: The function splits on '|', checks if parts[1] is a known severity, and returns parts[2] (the text after the prefix) if so.

claims.text: MEASURED: without this split, ``_resolve_store | medium | Mentions refusing paths under memory/ but code is truncated; the check may be missing`` was scored provably false because ``_resolve_store`` is defined -- but the finding never claimed otherwise. It is about a check INSIDE that function. Reading the location column as the subject manufactures a lie out of an honest observation.
claims.why: The example refers to _resolve_store and a scoring outcome, but this chunk does not contain _resolve_store or the scoring logic that produced the measured result. The claim about the example's behavior cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Verdicts: ``false`` the named symbol is defined in the module it is claimed absent from
claims.why: The code returns 'false' when hits is non-empty, where hits are named symbols that are in the module's defined set and not in the borrowed set.

claims.text: Verdicts: ``false-elsewhere`` it exists, in another module -- wrong about WHERE, which is a different error needing a different repair
claims.why: The code returns 'false-elsewhere' when every named symbol exists in at least one module's defined set (everywhere is non-empty), even if not in the current module.

claims.text: Verdicts: ``scoped`` the claim limits itself to the window its reader saw, so it asserts nothing about the program
claims.why: The code returns 'scoped' when _SELF_SCOPED.search(text) matches, indicating the claim is limited to the window.

claims.text: Verdicts: ``undecided`` this cannot tell. **Not a pass.**
claims.why: The code returns 'undecided' in all remaining paths: when the text is not an existence claim, when the module is not in the index, when the named symbol is imported (not defined), or when no named symbol resolves.

claims.text: It can prove a finding false. It can never prove one true.
claims.why: The function only returns 'false' or 'false-elsewhere' for negative proofs; there is no code path that returns a 'true' verdict. The claim is consistent with the observable returns.

observations.what: The docstring's MEASURED example references _resolve_store and a scoring outcome, but this chunk does not contain that function or the scoring logic; the example's validity cannot be checked from this chunk.
The judge docstring lists only four verdicts (false, false-elsewhere, scoped, undecided) but the code returns various reason strings for 'undecided' that are not enumerated in the docstring.
The functions depend on module-level constants _SEVERITIES, _NAME, _ABSENCE, and _SELF_SCOPED, which are not defined in this chunk. Their presence is implied but not verifiable here.
The judge function uses `defined.values()` to check existence elsewhere, which assumes the mapping values are iterables of symbols. This is consistent with the type hints.
